investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner produced zero evidence — all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler reports "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and "4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector," meaning no node in the 6-node cluster can accept a new remote agent pod. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"). This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never receives a running VM, so no evidence is written and the expected-output contract is fully violated.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's required node affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes recently lost capacity (e.g., due to a scale-down, node failure, or resource limit change), the effective capacity dropped to zero.
Tertiary — cluster-level scale constraint: the cluster may not have auto-scaling configured for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource type, or the auto-scaler has not yet added new nodes to absorb demand.
Lower confidence — concurrent eval runs or leaked agent VMs from prior eval runs consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without being cleaned up, leaving none for new probe attempts.

investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was 334 minutes old when the eval ran at 2026-07-06T10:24:11.570Z, meaning the last successful workflow publish occurred approximately 5 hours 34 minutes before the eval, exceeding the 300-minute (5-hour) freshness contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482. Less likely: The workflow ran and completed but the published artifact at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was not updated due to a GitHub Pages deployment lag or caching issue, causing the eval to read a stale version.
Least likely: A misconfiguration in the workflow schedule (e.g., cron expression drift or timezone mismatch) caused the workflow to run less frequently than the 300-minute contract requires.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner produced zero evidence — all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler reports "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and "4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector," meaning no node in the 6-node cluster can accept a new remote agent pod. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"). This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never receives a running VM, so no evidence is written and the expected-output contract is fully violated.

investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was 334 minutes old when the eval ran at 2026-07-06T10:24:11.570Z, meaning the last successful workflow publish occurred approximately 5 hours 34 minutes before the eval, exceeding the 300-minute (5-hour) freshness contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482.
